purpose: To consider consultation responses
content:
To consider consultation responses

1. 
That 12 responses from Bevington Street, 7 responses from
Gallery Road and 13 responses from Tilson Close, received as
summarised in Appendix 1, during
the informal review
consultation for the Parking Amendments in said roads, be
considered.
 
2. 
That it be approved to proceed to statutory consultation for the
parking amendments in Bevington Street, which includes the
introduction of Stop and Shop parking bays, free 30 minutes,
between the hours of 08.30 to 23:00, maximum stay 2 hours, no
return within 2 hours.
 
3. 
That it be approved to proceed to statutory consultation on the
amended proposals for double yellow lines on the bends in Gallery
Road, as shown in Appendix 2, with all other proposed double yellow
lines to progress.
 
4. 
That it be approved to abandon the proposals to introduce resident
parking in Tilson Close due to low levels of support from the
public for the scheme.
 
5. 
That it be noted that a further report will be brought to the
Leader should there be any valid statutory objections to the
traffic orders required to implement the amendments to the parking
schemes listed between recommendations 1-3. Should there
not be any valid statutory objections the schemes will be
implemented as proposed.
 
6. 
That it be noted that requests for any complementary measures will
be passed to the appropriate officers so that these can be
considered as per the relevant processes and procedures.

purpose:

traffic and highway improvements including parking regime
changes
content:
To implement non-strategic
traffic and highway improvements including parking regime
changes

1. 
That the non-strategic
traffic and highway improvements and complementary street space
measures detailed in appendix 1 - 29 annexed to this report and
summarised in Table 1, be
approved.  These are to be implemented
by way of powers under the Highways Act 1980 (“1980
Act”) and Traffic Management Orders (TMOs)  made under the Road Traffic Regulation Act
(“1984 Act”), subject to the outcome of a statutory
consultation and any associated procedures.
 
2. 
That officers be
authorized to undertake the statutory consultation process in
respect of the proposed Traffic Management Orders
(“TMOs”), including the publication of the necessary
notices and consideration of any representations received in
accordance with sections 6 and 124 (and the other relevant powers
identified in this report) of the 1984 Act subject to statutory
consultation carried out pursuant to the Local Authorities Traffic
Orders (Procedure) (England and Wales) Regulations 1996
(“1996 Regulations”).
 
3.

following the close of the statutory consultation period, officers
will submit a further report to the Leader should any
objections be received during the statutory consultation period
that have not subsequently been withdrawn. If no objections are
received, delegated authority is granted to the Head of Highways to
authorise the making of the
orders.
 
4. 
That officers be
authorized to take steps to hold a public inquiry pursuant to
regulation 9(1) of the 1996 Regulations in relation to the proposed
TMOs if considered expedient to do so.

purpose:
To determine the objections received during
the TMO statutory consultation process to formally notify decision
makers of the planned consolidation and digitisation of all Traffic
Management Orders (TMOs) onto the Mapper system, including Moving
Orders, in line with the Government D-TRO mandate.
content:
To determine the objections received during
the TMO statutory consultation process to formally notify decision
makers of the planned consolidation and digitisation of all Traffic
Management Orders (TMOs) onto the Mapper system, including Moving
Orders, in line with the Government D-TRO mandate.

1. 
That the background to
the Digitisation of Traffic Management Orders (TMOs) project as set
out in this report be noted.  The
statutory obligation arises under the Traffic Orders and Notices
(Provision of Digital Information) (England) Regulations 2025
(D-TRO Regulations 2025) pursuant to section 93 of the Automated
Vehicles Act 2024 (the 2024 Act), under which, Southwark Council
(the Council), together with all local authorities, is required to
fully digitise all of its TMOs by the Department for Transport
(DfT).
 
2. 
That it be noted that
a statutory consultation advertising the new orders was advertised
between 16 July to 6 August 2026, comprising new on-street static
TMOs  (including orders relating to
moving traffic, speed limits, and housing estate and other
off-street parking restrictions), in accordance with the statutory
procedure set out in the Local Authorities' Traffic Orders
(Procedure) (England and Wales) Regulations 1996 ("the 1996
Regulations").
 
3. 
That it be noted that
a statutory consultation was carried out with the bodies and
persons specified in regulation 6 of the 1996 Regulations, and with
the chief officer of police pursuant to paragraph 20 of Schedule 9
to the Road Traffic Regulation Act 1984 ("the 1984 Act"), before
any TMOs are made.
 
4. 
That it be noted that no representations were received during the
consultation.
 
5. 
That the making of the
above new orders and for the Council to become fully digitised with
its TMOs as per DfT requirements, be approved.
 
6. 
That the transition of
Temporary Traffic Management Orders (TTROs) to a digital format in
compliance with the D-TRO Regulations 2025 being implemented by the
DfT, be noted.

purpose:
To authorise officers to implement the permanent Traffic
Management Orders necessary for the Lower Road Safety Improvements
scheme (C4) and to revoke and/or modify the existing Traffic
Management Orders.
content:
To authorise officers to implement the permanent Traffic
Management Orders necessary for the Lower Road Safety Improvements
scheme (C4) and to revoke and/or modify the existing Traffic
Management Orders.





 

1. 
That the 223
representations received during the statutory consultation on the
proposed Lower Road C4 scheme, which includes bus priority
measures, cycle lanes, waiting and loading restrictions,
banned-turn movement restrictions and changes to parking provision
on Lower Road, be considered. The consultation was formally
advertised under reference TMO2526-042, and the representations are
summarised in paragraphs 21-28 and set out in full in Appendix
2.
 
2. 
That the officer
responses to the grounds of objection raised in relation to the
proposed Lower Road C4 scheme be considered, as summarised in
paragraph 29 and set out in detail in Appendix 1.
 
3. 
That officers be
authorized to make the permanent Traffic Management Orders referred
to in paragraph 16 of this report and to revoke and/or modify the
existing Traffic Management Orders referred to in paragraph 17.
These Orders shall be made, revoked and/or modified in accordance
with the Road Traffic Regulation Act 1984 (the 1984 Act) and the
Local Authorities’ Traffic Orders (Procedure) (England and
Wales) Regulations 1996 (the 1996 Regulations).
 
4. 
That it be noted that
the scheme is currently operating under Temporary Traffic
Management Orders (TTMOs). As the TTMOs were due to expire on 28
May 2026, they have been extended for six months, from 29 May 2026
to 28 November 2026, to maintain the existing arrangements pending
a decision on the proposed permanent scheme.
 
5. 
That officers be
instructed to notify all individuals and organisations who made
representations, informing them of the Council’s
decision.
 
6. 
That officers be
instructed to write to local communities to inform them of the
Council’s decision on the scheme, provide updates on the
Surrey Quays Gyratory scheme in due course, and prepare a
monitoring and evaluation plan for the Lower Road C4 scheme.
Officers shall continue to engage with ward councillors and the
wider community to monitor the scheme and identify opportunities to
improve bus performance and reduce congestion.

content:
To
approve:

· 
the formal advertising of the proposed new TMOs,
comprising new on-street static TMOs; and

· 
the transition of
Temporary Traffic Management Orders (TTROs) to a digital format in
compliance with the (D-TRO Regulations 2025).

The Leader of the Council approved the
following:
 
1.  The
background to the Digitisation of Traffic Management Orders (TMOs)
project as set out in this report.  The
statutory obligation arises under the Traffic Orders and Notices
(Provision of Digital Information) (England) Regulations 2025
(D-TRO Regulations 2025) pursuant to section 93 of the Automated
Vehicles Act 2024 (the 2024 Act). 
Further, Southwark Council (the Council) must have regard to the
October 2026 timeframe currently indicated by the Department for
Transport to digitise all TMOs be noted.
 
2.  Approval
be given for the formal advertising of the proposed new TMOs ,
comprising new on-street static TMOs 
(including orders relating to moving traffic, speed limits, and
housing estate and other off-street parking restrictions), in
accordance with the statutory procedure set out in the Local
Authorities' Traffic Orders (Procedure) (England and Wales)
Regulations 1996 ("the 1996 Regulations").
 
3.  That a
statutory consultation will be carried out with the bodies and
persons specified in regulation 6 of the 1996 Regulations, and with
the chief officer of police pursuant to paragraph 20 of Schedule 9
to the Road Traffic Regulation Act 1984 ("the 1984 Act"), before
any TMOs are made.
 
4.  All
representations and objections received during the statutory
consultation period would be fully considered before any decision
is taken to make the proposed TMOs.
 
5.  That a
further separate report would be brought before the Leader
following the close of the statutory consultation period, in all
cases, whether or not any objections are received to make a further
decision.
 
6.  That no
TMOs will be made as a result of this decision, and that the making
of any new TMOs remains subject to the Leader’s further
decision following the statutory consultation.
 
7.  Approval
be given for the transition of Temporary Traffic Management Orders
(TTROs) to a digital format in compliance with the (D-TRO
Regulations 2025) being implemented by the Department for
Transport.
topline: The Leader of the Council has decided to approve the formal advertising of new Traffic Management Orders and the transition of Temporary Traffic Management Orders to a digital format.

decision_maker: Cabinet Member for Climate Emergency, Jobs and Transport
purpose:
To implement a School Street in Victory
Primary School (Elba Place) introducing timed road closures during
school start and finish times to improve safety and air
quality.
content:
To implement a School Street in Victory
Primary School (Elba Place) introducing timed road closures during
school start and finish times to improve safety and air
quality.

1. 
That the School Street
proposal detailed in the design drawing to this report and
summarised below, implemented by way of powers under the Highways
Act 1980 (“the 1980 Act”), the Road Traffic Regulation
Act 1984 (“the 1984 Act”), and orders made under the
1984 Act, subject to the outcome of any necessary statutory
consultation and procedures, be approved.
 
2. 
That officers be
instructed to make the necessary Traffic Management Orders
(“TMOs”) in accordance with sections 6 and 124 of the
1984 Act, subject to statutory consultation carried out pursuant to
the Local Authorities Traffic Orders (Procedure) (England and
Wales) Regulations 1996 (“the 1996
Regulations”).
 
3. 
That officers be
instructed to carry out the necessary statutory consultation for
the proposed School Street at Victory Primary School in accordance
with the 1984 Act and all relevant statutory
requirements.
 
4. 
That it be noted that,
in the event objections to the TMOs for the proposed School Street
at Victory Primary School are received following statutory
consultation, a further report will be presented to the Cabinet
Member for determination.
topline: The Cabinet Member for Climate Emergency, Jobs and Transport has decided to implement a School Street at Victory Primary School to improve safety and air quality

To consider the non-strategic traffic and
highway improvements and complementary streetspace measures

1. 
That the non-strategic
traffic and highway improvements and complementary streetspace
measures detailed in the appendices to this report and summarised
in Table 1, implemented by way of powers under the Highways Act
1980 (“1980 Act”) and orders made under the Road
Traffic Regulation Act (“1984 Act”), subject to the
outcome of any necessary statutory consultation and procedures, be
approved.
 
2. 
That officers be
instructed to make the necessary Traffic Management Orders
(“TMOs”) in accordance with sections 6 and 124 (and the
other relevant powers identified in this report) of the 1984 Act
subject to statutory consultation carried out pursuant to the Local
Authorities Traffic Orders (Procedure) (England and Wales)
Regulations 1996 (“1996 Regulations”).
 
3. 
That the Equality
Impact Needs Analysis set out in this report in accordance with the
council’s Public Sector Equality Duty (“PSED”),
be considered.

a further report will be presented to the Cabinet Member to
determine whether to proceed with the making of the
TMOs.

public inquiry in the event objections are received related to any
of the proposed TMOs following statutory consultation pursuant to
Regulation 9(1) of the 1996 Regulations.
 
6. 
That officers be
authorised to carry out the necessary statutory notification in
accordance with sections 90A to 90F of the 1980 Act and the
Highways (Road Humps) Regulations 1999 (“1999
Regulations”).
 
7. 
That officers be authorised to
exercise discretion as to whether or not to hold a public inquiry
in the event objections are received in respect of the proposed
traffic calming measures (“road humps”) in accordance
with section 90C(4) of the 1980 Act.

purpose:
To enter into an agreement
under Section 113 of the Local Government Act 1972 to provide
Pensions and Treasury services to Bexley Council.
content:
To enter into an agreement
under Section 113 of the Local Government Act 1972 to provide
Pensions and Treasury services to Bexley Council.

1. 
That the establishment
of a two-way shared Pensions and Treasury service with the London
Borough of Bexley (Bexley) pursuant to Section 113 of the Local
Government Act 1972, with London Borough of Southwark (Southwark)
acting as the host authority, for a period of three years, with the
option to extend by two further years, with a commencement date of
1 April 2026, be approved.
 
2. 
That the annual fees
to be charged by Southwark to Bexley for the Pensions and Treasury
service, to increase annually in line with national pay awards be
approved.
 
3. 
That the establishment
of four new permanent roles to resource the shared service
specification for the Pensions and Treasury service, with these
being fully funded by the fees charged by Southwark to Bexley be
approved.
 
4. 
That the terms of the
authority agreement at Appendix 1 of the closed version of the
report be agreed.
 
5. 
That it be noted that
the arrangement includes the appointment by Southwark of an Interim
Pensions Officer to complete Bexley’s 2025-2026 pension fund
accounts and annual report prior to the commencement date of 1
April 2026, with all associated costs to be fully reimbursed by
Bexley to Southwark, and that this arrangement shall be covered by
the authority agreement.
 
6. 
That it be noted that
there are no identified Transfer of Undertakings (Protection of
Employment) Regulations 2006 (TUPE) matters to consider in respect
of this arrangement.
 
7. 
That it be noted that
officers in Bexley are presenting a report to their respective
authority in relation to this arrangement.
 
8. 
That it be noted that
Bexley’s current shared service arrangement with another
London borough will end on 31 March 2026 and that the agreement
with Southwark must commence on 1 April 2026 to ensure continuity
of service.
topline: The Strategic Director of Resources has decided to enter into an agreement to provide Pensions and Treasury services to Bexley Council.

content:
To approve the implementation of the proposed
designs on Lower Road from Culling Road to the section before
Surrey Quays Road and Chiltern Grove junction.

 

That officers be instructed to proceed
with the detailed design stage and undertake the statutory
consultation prior to implementing any permanent Traffic Management
Order (TMO) necessary for the Lower Road Safety Improvements
scheme. Any subsequent decision to make permanent TMOs would rely
on the Council’s powers under the Highways Act 1980
(“1980 Act”) and sections 6, 49(5), 63 and 124 of the
Road Traffic Regulation Act 1984 (“RTRA”). The Council
would also discharge its duties under sections 45 and the 122 of
the RTRA if, following statutory consultation, a decision was taken
to proceed with making a permanent TMO. However, before any
decision can be made on whether to introduce a permanent TMO to
implement this scheme – and to replace the current temporary
traffic orders introduced as part of the 2025 road layout (Part B
Appendix 1) – a statutory consultation must be carried out,
in accordance with the Local Authorities Traffic Orders (Procedure)
(England and Wales) Regulations 1996 (“1996
Regulations”).

 

That it be approved to proceed with
statutory consultation on the proposed removal of the
right-turn bans at Culling Road and Ann Moss
Way.

 

That it be noted that the following
amendment will be subject to the outcome of statutory advertisement
of the required TMOs:

· 
Amended layouts at
Culling Road and Ann Moss Way (Part D Appendix 1)
· 
Chilton Grove junction
safety improvements (Part C Appendix 1)
· 
Implementation of a
yellow box junction at Redriff
Road
· 
Kerb realignment in the cycle track near
Orange Place
 

That the safety-critical “Amended
road safety improvements” layout outlined in Table 4 (and
Part D Appendix 1) be agreed for the purposes of statutory
consultation.

 

That officers be authorised to continue monitoring the scheme and
engage with the community to identify further measures to improve
bus performance and reduce congestion.

Gibbon Road, Half Moon Lane and Monnow Road

and complementary streetspace measures
detailed in the appendices to the report and summarised in Table 1,
implemented by way of powers under the Highways Act 1980
(“1980 Act”) and orders made under the Road Traffic
Regulation Act (“1984 Act”), subject to the outcome of
any necessary statutory consultation and procedures be approved by
the Cabinet Member for Clean Air, Streets and Waste.
 
2. 
Necessary Traffic Management Orders
(“TMOs”) in accordance with sections 6 and 124 (and the
other relevant powers identified in this report) of the 1984 Act
subject to statutory consultation carried out pursuant to the Local
Authorities Traffic Orders (Procedure) (England and Wales)
Regulations 1996 (“1996 Regulations”) by officers
instructed by the Cabinet Member for Clean Air, Streets and
Waste.
 
3. 
The equalities assessment set out in this report in
accordance with the council’s Public Sector Equality Duty
(“PSED”) be considered by the Cabinet Member for Clean
Air, Streets and Waste.
 

In the event objections are received
following statutory consultation, a further report will be
presented to the Cabinet Member in order for him to determine
whether to proceed with the making of the TMOs be noted by the
Cabinet Member for Clean Air, Streets and Waste.

 

Discretion as to whether or not to hold a
public inquiry in the event objections are received related to any
of the proposed TMOs following statutory consultation pursuant to
Regulation 9(1) of the 1996 Regulations be exercised by officers as
authorised by the Cabinet Member for Clean Air, Streets and
Waste.

 

Officers carry out the necessary statutory
notification in accordance with sections 90A to 90F of the 1980 Act
and the Highways (Road Humps) Regulations 1999 (“1999
Regulations”) as authorised by the Cabinet Member for Clean
Air, Streets and Waste.

 

Officers to exercise discretion as to
whether or not to hold a public inquiry in the event objections are
received in respect of the proposed traffic calming measures
(“road humps”) in accordance with section 90C(4) of the
1980 Act as authorised by the Cabinet Member for Clean Air, Streets
and Waste.

purpose:

content:
To approve phase 2 of the Tustin Estate
renewal

Cabinet heard representations
from Andrew Eke, chair of tenants and residents association.
 
RESOLVED:
 

1. 
That it be noted that since the development
agreement was signed in October 2022, the Tustin Estate Renewal has
been progressing well on site, and that Phase 1 is about to
complete and will deliver 167 new homes, including 157 council
homes for social rent, and 10 homes for resident
leaseholders.

 

2. 
That it be agreed that the strategy for delivering
Phase 2 should change to accelerate the delivery of affordable
housing as set out in paragraphs 38-51 of the report.
 

3. 
That it be agreed that 98 homes that were previously
intended to be key worker homes for London Living Rent should be
changed to deliver additional new council homes for social
rent.
 

4. 
That it be noted that the Greater London Authority
(GLA) have agreed to provide grant funding for these 98 additional
council homes, if the tenure change is agreed.

 

5. 
That it be agreed that to start Phase 2, the council
will enter into an early works contract in the sum of
£10,667,678 for a period of six months commencing December
2025 to finalise the detailed Phase 2 design work and to demolish
Kentmere House and Heversham House, ahead of demolition starting in
March 2026 (subject to vacant possession being
achieved).
 

6. 
That it be noted that the main works contract will
include the construction of all four blocks within Phase 2, but
will include separate prices for the development of each of the
four blocks within Phase 2, with Phase 2a including Block G2, and a
break clause that can be exercised before the end of October 2026
to exclude Phase 2b which is made up of Blocks F1, F2 and
H.
 

7. 
That it be noted that a subsequent report will be
presented to cabinet in early 2026 to confirm the final price for
Phase 2a main works, and an updated estimate for Phase 2b main
works, and to agree that Bouygues Development should enter into a construction contract to deliver
them.
 

8. 
That the updated total estimated cost to deliver
Phase 2 of the Tustin Estate Renewal as set out in the closed
version of the report be noted.
 

9. 
That a minor variation is made to the development
agreement in line with the points set out in paragraph 53 of the
report to accommodate the Building Safety Act changes.
topline: The Cabinet has decided to approve phase 2 of the Tustin Estate renewal, changing the strategy to accelerate the delivery of affordable housing and reallocating key worker homes to additional council homes for social rent.

purpose:
To consider the future of Marie
Curie House
content:
To consider the future of Marie
Curie House

Cabinet heard representations
from Mike Edge, chair of tenants and residents association and ward
councillors Ian Wingfield, Ellie Cumbo and Jason Ochere.
 
RESOLVED:
 
1. 
That the recommendations in the report to scrutiny
committee on 14 October (Appendix 1 of the report) including the
recommendation to demolish the residential block known as Marie
Curie and the need to consider appropriate steps to address the
findings of the recent Type 4 Fire Risk Assessment in 2025
(Appendix 2 of the report) be noted.
 
2. 
That the departure from the original approved 2022
cabinet recommendation to undertake Phase 2 fire safety works and
remediation be noted. The recommendation not to proceed with the
original approval reflects the impact of updated fire safety
regulations, the recommendations from the recent structural
engineering report, the introduction of a new compliance sign-off
process for high-rise buildings, ongoing market volatility,
inflationary pressures, and sustained financial strain on the
housing revenue account (HRA).
 
3. 
That it be noted that Marie Curie and Lakanal House
are sister blocks situated within the Sceaux Gardens Estate. They
exhibit comparable architectural characteristics, notably their
duplex 'scissors flat' configuration and concrete frame
construction. Nevertheless, the context surrounding decision-making
and the implementation of safety measures for each block varies
considerably as set out in the report.
 
4. 
That the progress with the resident engagement and
rehousing of residents and buy backs of leaseholder properties has
progressed and that all tenants have been offered the right to
return be noted.
 
5. 
That the outcome of the independent structural
engineering report on the Marie Curie block that identifies
emerging issues ranging from structural degradation due to
humidity, insufficient reinforcement bar cover and the building
nearing or exceeding its original design life, highlighting the
need for decisive intervention be noted.
 
6. 
That it be noted that if a decision to approve
demolition is agreed by cabinet that the procurement of a
demolition contractor for Marie Curie will be subject to a separate
GW1 and GW2 process in line with the council’s gateway
process.
 
7. 
That to maintain continuity for residents, estate
and key stakeholders, the proposal is to include the Marie Curie
scheme together with the Florian and Racine sites on the Sceaux
Gardens Estate in the pipeline sites as part of the Southwark
Construction Development Agreement (DA) Future Programme for new
homes, subject to separate approval from the cabinet member for new
homes and sustainable development in consultation with strategic
director of housing, strategic director of resources and director
of planning and growth be noted.
 
8. 
That it be noted that the demolition is subject to
the council obtaining ballot exemption from the Greater London
Authority (GLA) as set out in paragraphs 68 to 70 of the
report.
 
9. 
That the estimated cost for the demolition works as
set out in paragraph 13 of the report be noted. This will be
subject to additional approval to vary the housing investment
programme.
 
10. 
That subject to paragraphs 8 and 9 of the report,
the demolition of the Marie Curie block, following its review by
the housing scrutiny committee be approved, noting that all
alternative options have been thoroughly assessed, with demolition
identified as the most cost-effective and practicable solution as
detailed in paragraphs 31 to 43 of the report.

decision_maker: Deputy Leader and Cabinet Member for Children, Education and Refugees
purpose: Grant funding
content:
Grant funding

That the Deputy Leader and Cabinet Member
for Children, Education & Refugees

Approves the proposed model whereby United
St Saviours will manage the Voluntary and Community Sector (VCS)
Borough of Sanctuary grant funding for years 2, 3, and 4
(2025-2028) on behalf of Southwark Council. United St Saviours will
consider providing additional funding to support the initiative,
though no firm commitment can be made at this time.
Notes that one key
benefit of management by United St Saviours is that the Council can
access trust-based grant-making, empowering organisations
supporting refugees, migrants, and asylum seekers with flexible,
inclusive management. United St Saviours will not charge management
fees on this occasion.
Notes that the total commitment of
£300,000(£100,000 per annum for three years) will
continue to be met by existing government grants allocated to the
Council.

subsequently withdrawn) during the statutory
consultation.

and the equalities assessment set out in the report be considered
in accordance with the council’s Public Sector Equality Duty
(“PSED”).
